sentences.text:
Heard Sri Hemanth Kumar K., learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Mahesh Shetty, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1.
3.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has remained absent throughout and this Court noticing his absence, on 12.06.2023, has passed the following order:
This Court on 10.08.2022, had passed the following order:
"This Court on 06.04.2022, had passed the following order:
"Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners.
Though respondent No.2 is represented by Sri H.R.Raghu, learned counsel, has not appeared on both the occasions i.e., forenoon and afternoon.
In the interest of justice, list the matter on 08.04.2022.
In the event, learned counsel for respondent No.2 would not appear on the next date of hearing, the matter would be taken in his absence.

Interim order granted earlier, is extended till the next date of hearing."
Yet again, on 07.06.2022, this Court passed the following order:
"Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader.
Respondent No.2 was not represented on 06.04.2022 and remains absent even today.
Therefore, as a last chance, list this matter on 14.06.2022.
In the event, learned counsel for respondent No.2 would not appear, the matter would be decided in his absence."
On both occasions, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 was not present.
As a last chance, list the matter on 17.08.2022.
In the event, learned counsel for respondent No.2 would not appear on the aforesaid date, the matter would be taken up and decided, in his absence.

Interim order granted earlier, is extended till the disposal of the petition."
Even today, there is no representation on behalf of respondent No.2 - complainant.
As a last chance, list the matter on 21.06.2023.
In the event, respondent No.2 would not be represented the matter, the matter would be heard and disposed.

Even today, there is no representation on behalf of respondent No.2.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader are heard in the matter.

4. Brief facts of the case, germane for consideration of the issue in the lis, are as follows:
Respondent Nos.2 is the complainant.

The petitioners accused Nos.1 to 3 are purchasers of the property bearing khata No.1634/1 measuring 30 x 50 ft. situated at Belavadi Village, Illavala Hobli, Mysuru, from the hands of the father of the complainant.
The petitioners come in possession of the subject property in terms of a sale deed dated 21.08.2009, executed by the father of the complainant.
Against her father, the complainant then institute a civil suit in O.S.No.744/2015 seeking partition in the property, in which the complainant claims that she is entitled to.
The said suit is claimed to be pending adjudication even as on date.

After filing of the said suit and finding no order being passed in her favour in the said NC: 2023:KHC:21548 suit, registers a private complaint under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. in P.C.R.No.96/2017 for the offences under Sections 415 and 420 r/w. 34 of the IPC.
The learned Magistrate refers the matter for investigation to the jurisdictional police under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C., which then becomes a crime in crime No.66/2017.
The police after investigation file a 'B' summary report before the concerned Court.
The complainant files objections to the 'B' summary report.

The concerned Court considering the 'B' summary report and the objections of the complainant, rejects the 'B' summary report and takes cognizance of the offences under Sections 415 and 420 of the IPC.
Taking cognizance by the learned Magistrate is what drives the petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners would contend that the petitioners are bonafide purchasers from the hands of the father of the complainant, who is their vendor.
The sale takes place on 21.08.2009, in which the complainant claims her share in the property, which is the subject property of O.S.No.744/2015.
The matter on the face of it, which is purely NC: 2023:KHC:21548 civil in nature is sought to be given a colour of crime and seek quashment of the proceedings.

6. Learned High Court Government Pleader on the other hand, would toe the lines of the learned counsel for the petitioners as the police have filed 'B' summary report on the ground that the matter is purely civil in nature.
7. As observed hereinabove, complainant No.2 remains absent throughout.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and have perused the material on record.

sentences.text: 9. The afore-narrated facts are not in dispute and requires no reiteration.
The petitioners come in possession of the property on 21.08.2009, in terms of the sale deed executed by one Shivanna, the father of the complainant.

The complainant has the grievance against her father with regard to NC:
2023:KHC:21548 the partition of the property and on such grievance, instituted a civil suit in O.S.No.744/2015.
In the civil suit, no interim order of stay / direction is granted in favour of the complainant.
The complainant then takes an alternate route by setting up the criminal law in motion by filing a private complaint in P.C.R.No.96/2017, invoking Section 200 of the Cr.P.C.

The complaint is referred for investigation by the learned Magistrate under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C.
10.
It is then a crime, in Crime No.66/2017 is registered for the offences under Sections 415 and 420 r/w. 34 of the IPC.
The very registration of the crime for the offence under Section 415 of the IPC is erroneous as it is the definition of cheating.
The police filed the 'B' summary report and the concerned Court rejects the 'B' summary report and takes cognizance of the offences under Sections 415 and 420 of the IPC.
The very taking cognizance under Section 415 of the Cr.P.C. on the face of it is erroneous.
What remains is Section 420 of the IPC.
For an offence to become punishable under Section 420 of the IPC, its ingredients would necessarily have to be met.

The petitioners are the purchasers from the hands of one Shivanna; Shivanna is the father of the complainant; the complainant has the grievance against her father with regard to the partition of the property and the proceedings are at large before the concerned civil Court in O.S.No.744/2015.
12.

On the facts of the case, the petitioners have not induced the complainant to part with the property by cheating or dishonest intention which is sine qua non under Section 420 of the IPC to be prima facie met.
The petitioners have legally become the owners of the property pursuant to the sale deed executed by the father of the complainant on 21.08.2009.
If the daughter has grievance against her father and the grievance is pending before the concerned Court, the complainant has to pursue the proceedings before the concerned Court.

In a issue which is purely civil in nature,
registration of a crime under Section 420 of the IPC against the petitioners, who are the purchasers of the property on the face of it, is illegal.
Therefore, permitting proceedings to continue against the petitioners is an abuse of the process of the law and miscarriage of justice.

For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER a.
The criminal petition is allowed.

b. The order dated 25.11.2019 in P.C.R.No.96/2017 and the investigation /
proceedings in Crime No.66/2017, stand quashed.
